simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to מַכְמָר (H4364) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: מַכְמָר (makmâr) means a (hunter's) net (as dark from concealment) First listed occurrence: Isa 51 20.

definitions.full: H4364. makmar מִכְמָר noun [masculine] net, snare , bringing an animal to its fall, מ ׳כְּתוֺא Isa 51:20 like an antelope of ( in ) a net or snare (compare II. חֵרֶם , II. רֶשֶׁת ). [ מַכְמֹר ] noun [masculine] net, snare (see foregoing) — plural suffix רְשָׁעִים בְּמַכְמֹרָיו יִמְּלוּ Psa 141:10 ; so Gr Che 140:11 ( במכמרות for בְּמַהֲמֹרוֺת ᵑ0 , see).
definitions.rootNote: or מִכְמֹר ; from 3648 in the sense of blackening by heat;
